name: Permanent Residence Status

requirements.blocker_text: Progressed through a multi-year gradual status-upgrade process, most commonly via marriage to an Israeli citizen or long-term residence (e.g. East Jerusalem residents hold a distinct, historically rooted permanent-residence status not modeled in detail here).

evidence_required.document: Documentation of the qualifying track (marriage, long-term residence, etc.)

sources.title: Decker, Pex, Levi Law Firm (Israeli immigration law firm) -- permanent residency in Israel described generally as reached via a gradual status-upgrade process (commonly marriage-based) or as a distinct, historically rooted status held by East Jerusalem residents

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Israel). STATUS: DRAFT -- WEAK FILE, thin and entirely tier-3 sourced. Israel's permanent-residence system is unusually fragmented across distinct historical and legal tracks rather than one general 'years of temporary residence' route seen in most other countries in this dataset: East Jerusalem Palestinian residents hold a specific, long-standing form of permanent residency rooted in Israel's 1967 annexation of East Jerusalem (a status with its own extensive legal history around 'center of life' residency reviews and revocations, not modeled in requirement detail here given its complexity and the sourcing constraints of this pass); spouses of Israeli citizens can reach permanent residence via the family-reunification track (see il_family_reunification.json, including its statutory exclusions); and a small population may hold permanent residence via other historical routes. No single, general, nationality-neutral 'years of residence' permanent-residence route comparable to Botswana's or Jordan's Five-Year Residency was found for ordinary foreign residents without a family or historical basis -- disclosed as a genuine structural finding rather than papered over with an invented general track.
